title: Virtual fixed UInt64 views
objective: Implement fail-closed scalar replacement for local nonescaping fixed UInt64Buffer views in checked private graph variants, with portable emitted C and hostile mutation tests

oracles: Ordinary checked public UInt64Buffer view behavior
Generated C retains checked fallback unless compiler authority is reverified

handoff.summary: Implemented opt-in, compiler-authorized scalar replacement for local nonescaping UInt64Buffer views in checked private variants. Fixed views can omit proved construction; dynamic views retain exact construction-time validation and snapshot their data pointer and logical length. Proof groups are atomic and mutation-sensitive, while unsupported cases retain the ordinary checked path. Focused hostile and runtime tests pass for int64, uint64, and arbitrary-precision Integer inputs. The independent frozen Stage-E harness reached all 11 readable catalog views and matched 12 valid plus 27 malformed executions exactly, but timing was neutral at 1.002790x and 1.005683x the same-tip Stage-D control.
risks: Validated virtualization deliberately handles only top-level local views rooted directly in UInt64Buffer parameters; nested roots, escaping views, and structured construction retain ordinary checked descriptors.

pnpm test:changed stopped on unrelated native-cache lifecycle environment-key instability. pnpm test:compiler had pre-existing missing-FLINT-addon and generated Any ReferenceError failures; 17 compiler fixtures passed.

pnpm test:native reaches the IR-version ratchets but fails because the new capability advances generated IR from version 45 to 46; shared ratchet updates are deliberately excluded from this lane. With temporary local 46 expectations, all affected compiler-shape tests passed before the remaining native-kernel.cjs ratchet stopped the run.

The frozen catalog eliminated 22 UInt64 descriptor locals and all 11 descriptor data/length/offset assignments, reducing generated core by 2013 bytes, but did not reduce 67 signed index checks, 68 UInt64 bounds failures, or 275 checked int64 arithmetic sites. Addon size and ELF text were unchanged, explaining the neutral timing result.
next_steps: Do not pursue descriptor virtualization as the next performance campaign: it is semantically sound but the frozen result rejects it as the dominant remaining cost.
Target the unchanged logical index checks, checked int64 arithmetic, or private call/status ABI overhead with a separately proved transformation and a same-tip frozen benchmark.
